old_excerpt:
[opus-5, final message, turn 14]

"Both watchers are armed — I'll report when the run completes."

Training launched in the background; the agent ended its turn waiting to be called back. In headless one-shot mode no callback ever comes: report.json was never written and the task scored fail.
new_excerpt:
[fable-5-1, final message, turn 12]

"Waiting for both runs to complete. Nothing else is needed until the completion notification arrives."

Same mistake, independently: two training runs backgrounded (it even wrote make_report.py for afterwards), turn ended, no report. Both frontier models treat a one-shot headless run like an interactive session.
caption: The one failure both models share: interactive habits colliding with headless -p mode. Neither fabricated results — they both waited, honestly, for a callback that could never arrive.
